messages:
jdoe_customer: Hey team — planning an enterprise POC for Redwood Private (VPC). Setup is hub-and-spoke TGW + corporate egress proxy with TLS-inspect. Requirements: preserve client source IP for audit, static egress IP per region (BYOIP/EIP preferred), data residency in eu-west-1. Questions: 1) can PrivateLink preserve SRC IP or do we need a proxy? 2) If TLS-inspect is mandatory, how does that impact the design? 3) what is the pricing delta proxy vs PrivateLink? 4) any blockers for a 2-week POC starting next week?

mike_sales: Thanks — looping in Anya (solutions) and Sam (neteng) to scope tech + pricing.

anya_se: Quick clarifying q's before we propose options: a) is TLS MITM (terminate & re-encrypt) happening in your FW? b) can you host a transit VPC for egress EIP? c) expected RPS / avg token throughput?

jdoe_customer: Yes, TLS MITM on our firewall (terminate and re-encrypt). We can host the transit VPC. Expected ~50 rps peak, ~10 rps avg. Must keep data in eu-west-1.

sam_neteng: Short answer: PrivateLink by itself does NOT preserve original client source IP at the Redwood backend — traffic is seen from the ENI on our side. Options that meet your constraints:
1) PrivateLink + application-level forwarding: run a reverse proxy in your transit VPC (with BYOIP/EIP) that forwards X-Forwarded-For to Redwood. Gives static egress IP + audit trail.
2) VPC peering / shared VPC so src IPs are preserved natively — simpler for srcip but increases routing coupling and potential blast radius.
3) Reverse-proxy in your transit VPC + PrivateLink for isolation — recommended: static EIP on your proxy, TLS inspect there, then PrivateLink to our private endpoint.
Tradeoffs: PrivateLink = better isolation & whitelistability; peering = native srcip but requires more network policy work. For your TLS-inspect requirement option 3 is the least operational friction.

sam_neteng: Firewall / allowlist snippet (example) — we'll provide final IPs once we allocate POC endpoints:

```
# Example outbound allow rule (eu-west-1 POC)
# dst: replace with final Redwood-provided EIP(s)
dst: 3.120.45.67/32
port: 443
proto: TCP
fqdns: private-api.redwood.ai, *.redwood-inference.com
# SNI allowlist: allow TLS SNI values: "private-api.redwood.ai" and "*.redwood-inference.com"
```

anya_se: Pricing / ops note: Proxy path (we host or you host reverse-proxy with reserved EIP) has modest infra/setup cost — for Dedicated/private POC we typically estimate ~€150/day extra for reserved capacity + static egress NAT overhead (one-time setup fee possible). PrivateLink-only handoffs (no managed proxy) are cheaper on infra but may require more customer routing work. I'll put exact numbers in a short doc and share.

linda_sec: Security checklist: we'll need an Integration Assessment (IA) and an encryption-in-transit diagram showing where TLS is terminated and re-encrypted. If TLS inspect is present in the middle, mark which certificates Redwood will see. For key management: Redwood Private supports KMS integrations — confirm whether you require HSM-backed KMS.

deploy-bot: ticket#3421 created: sales > network-handoff > jdoe_poc. Assigned to sam_neteng. Preflight checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/poc-network-preflight (access required).

jdoe_customer: Thanks — we'll provision the transit VPC and attach an EIP (BYOIP-ready). Can you share the exact IP allowlist + a 1-page network diagram? Aim to start Thurs if you can provide final IPs by Wed EOD.

sam_neteng: We'll prepare the IP allowlist + diagram today and post here. Example curl test to validate SNI/egress path once you have the EIP: 

```
curl -v --resolve private-api.redwood.ai:443:3.120.45.67 https://private-api.redwood.ai/health
```

This verifies DNS/SNI resolves to the EIP and the service responds.

anya_se: I'll send a short pricing estimate and book a 30-min kickoff Thurs AM. :calendar:

jdoe_customer: Great, appreciate the quick triage. We'll share transit VPC CIDRs, route table contacts, and the compliance checklist by EOD.

sam_neteng: Noted — I'll post the diagram + final EIP list here once provisioned.
